summary: HTTP MCP must require an environment-supplied bearer token, publish that HTTP-only requirement separately from API auth, and verify the actual listener stays on loopback unless TLS is enabled.
reason: An unauthenticated HTTP listener can expose local job and learning data, and a requested hostname alone does not prove where plaintext traffic binds.
validated_outcome: Synthetic tests cover token rejection and acceptance, loopback-only plaintext, TLS configuration, and actual bound-address checks; catalog generator and MCPB manifest checks preserve API-only auth while listing the HTTP token.
